en.no_claim: Couldn't tell which company this claims to be from.
en.not_in_ledger: It claims to be from {name}, but {name} isn't in your ledger (the companies you actually use).
en.disguised: The link uses "@" or "\" to disguise where it goes. It actually goes to "{host}".
en.disguised_unreadable: The link uses "@" or "\" to disguise where it goes. Where it actually goes can't be read.
en.shortener: The link ({host}) is a shortened URL, so you can't see where it goes.
en.idn: The link "{host}" contains characters that normal web addresses don't use. This trick is used to make a fake address look real.
en.mimic: The link "{host}" is made to look like an address of {name}, but it isn't an official one.
en.off_domain: The link "{host}" isn't an official address of the company it claims to be from.
en.official: The link "{host}" matches an official address of {name}.
en.unknown_domain: The link "{host}" isn't one of the registered official addresses.
en.phone: There's a phone number in the message. There's no way to tell whether it's real. If you call, use a number you've checked yourself, such as on the official website or the back of your card.
en.takeover: A request often used to take over accounts: {list}. Real companies don't usually ask for this through a link in an email or text, or over the phone. Check in the official app yourself.
en.nothing_to_check: There was nothing to check this against: no company in your ledger and no link to an official address.
